title: The Life and, for Now, the Death of the Kennedy Center

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ时，你每晚都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，然后你会把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成一个活生生的、充满50年历史精美文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼带来的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，没错。

sentences.en: You know, this is what they play when the performance is about to start.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是演出即将开始时他们播放的音乐。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You're calling people in.
sentences.zh: 你在招呼大家入场。

sentences.en: So a few months ago, I took a tour of the Kennedy Center with a tour guide there.
sentences.zh: 几个月前，我请了一位导游带我参观了肯尼迪中心。

sentences.en: Oh, can I get your name?
sentences.zh: 哦，能告诉我你的名字吗？

sentences.en: Oh, Sandy Weiswasser.
sentences.zh: 哦，桑迪·韦斯瓦瑟。

sentences.en: A volunteer named Sandy Weiswasser.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫桑迪·韦斯瓦瑟的志愿者。

sentences.en: Wow, I gotta spell that out.
sentences.zh: 哇，我得拼一下这个名字。

sentences.en: W-E-I-S-W-A.
sentences.zh: W-E-I-S-W-A.

sentences.en: She's 87 years old.
sentences.zh: 她今年87岁了。

sentences.en: She's a huge bundle of energy.
sentences.zh: 她浑身充满了活力。

sentences.en: And for the last 20 years, she has given tours every single Monday.
sentences.zh: 在过去的20年里，她每个周一都会带人参观。

sentences.en: Are you an artist yourself?
sentences.zh: 你自己是艺术家吗？

sentences.en: Am I an artist?
sentences.zh: 我是艺术家吗？

sentences.en: No, I play the piano, though.
sentences.zh: 不，不过我会弹钢琴。

sentences.en: You do?
sentences.zh: 你会吗？

sentences.en: And I hear a lot about the arts.
sentences.zh: 而且我听过很多关于艺术的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, I love ballet and opera.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我热爱芭蕾和歌剧。

sentences.en: Before President Trump took over the Kennedy Center, Sandy's tours were always packed.
sentences.zh: 在特朗普总统接管肯尼迪中心之前，桑迪的参观团总是人满为患。

sentences.en: But then he took over, made a lot of changes, and people stopped coming.
sentences.zh: 但后来他接管了这里，做了很多改变，人们就不再来了。

sentences.en: And so on the day that I was there, the center was empty, and I was the only person on Sandy's tour.
sentences.zh: 所以在我去的那天，中心空荡荡的，我是桑迪参观团里唯一的人。

sentences.en: So this foyer apparently is one of the largeSt...
sentences.zh: 所以这个门厅显然是最大的……

sentences.en: And as she walked me through the center...
sentences.zh: 当她带我穿过中心时……

sentences.en: The largest gift is this marble, which comes from Carrara, Italy.
sentences.zh: 最大的礼物是这块大理石，它来自意大利卡拉拉。

sentences.en: It's a beautiful chandelier.
sentences.zh: 这是一盏美丽的吊灯。

sentences.en: It's done by Dale Chihuly.
sentences.zh: 它是戴尔·奇胡利的作品。

sentences.en: It was clear how proud she was of the place.
sentences.zh: 很明显，她对这个地方感到多么自豪。

sentences.en: I like the undulating quality of it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它那种起伏的质感。

sentences.en: And how much she reveres it.
sentences.zh: 以及她对这里有多么崇敬。

sentences.en: No bed seat in the place.
sentences.zh: 这里连个座位都没有。

sentences.en: No, it doesn't look like it.
sentences.zh: 不，看起来确实没有。

sentences.en: But at some point in the tour, it occurred to me that she was speaking in the past tense.
sentences.zh: 但在参观的某个时刻，我突然意识到她一直在用过去时态说话。

sentences.en: You know, that's the other thing when I give my tours now.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是我现在带参观团时遇到的另一个问题。

sentences.en: Do I give them present tense or past tense?
sentences.zh: 我该用现在时还是过去时来介绍？

sentences.en: It's very hard.
sentences.zh: 这很难。

sentences.en: What words to use for my verbs?
sentences.zh: 我的动词该用什么词？

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 总之。

sentences.en: And the tour she was giving was kind of a tour of wreckage.
sentences.zh: 她所进行的参观，更像是一场关于残骸的巡礼。

sentences.en: And what she was explaining in all of her memories started to sound a lot to me like a eulogy.
sentences.zh: 她在所有回忆中解释的内容，听起来越来越像是一篇悼词。

sentences.en: So, I mean, all these little things about all the performers that are no longer here is very sad.
sentences.zh: 我是说，所有关于那些不再出现在这里的表演者的小事，都让人感到非常悲伤。

sentences.en: And it also became clear that in Sandy's mind, there was one person responsible for all that had happened to the Kennedy Center.
sentences.zh: 而且也变得很清楚，在桑迪看来，有一个人要为肯尼迪中心发生的一切负责。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, this place used to be really thriving and busy and crowded.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这个地方曾经非常繁荣、繁忙且拥挤。

sentences.en: Now it's very empty.
sentences.zh: 现在却非常空旷。

sentences.en: And that was President Trump.
sentences.zh: 那个人就是特朗普总统。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, the life and for the time being, the death of the Kennedy Center.
sentences.zh: 今天，肯尼迪中心的生命，以及目前为止，它的死亡。

sentences.en: My colleague, Elizabeth Williamson, brings us the story of how President Trump decided to take over and now shut down Washington's biggest and most celebrated home for the arts.
sentences.zh: 我的同事伊丽莎白·威廉姆森为我们讲述了特朗普总统如何决定接管，并最终关闭了华盛顿最大、最著名的艺术殿堂的故事。

sentences.en: It's Friday, September 25th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月25日，星期五。

sentences.en: Elizabeth, welcome back to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白，欢迎回到《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Michael, it's great to join you.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，很高兴能加入你。

sentences.en: You have been watching the Kennedy Center shut down for months, first gradually and then abruptly, when it literally closed its doors about 10 days ago.
sentences.zh: 你已经观察肯尼迪中心关闭好几个月了，起初是逐渐关闭，然后是突然关闭，大约10天前它彻底关门了。

sentences.en: So we're coming to you for what feels a bit like a post-mortem here, to understand why President Trump has closed this place down.
sentences.zh: 所以我们来找你，进行一场类似尸检的讨论，以了解特朗普总统为什么要关闭这个地方。

sentences.en: And I think any good post-mortem has to begin with the question of motivation.
sentences.zh: 我认为任何好的尸检都必须从动机问题开始。

sentences.en: How do you think about his motivation here?
sentences.zh: 你认为他在这里的动机是什么？

sentences.en: I think you have to go back to President Trump's first term.
sentences.zh: 我认为你必须回顾特朗普总统的第一个任期。

sentences.en: Remember, this was a really brutal election with a surprise result.
sentences.zh: 记住，那是一场非常残酷的选举，结果令人惊讶。

sentences.en: He comes into the White House.
sentences.zh: 他入主白宫。

sentences.en: He had been roundly rejected by cultural elites in New York City, the epicenter of the nation's cultural life.
sentences.zh: 他遭到了纽约市文化精英的彻底排斥，而纽约市是全国文化生活的中心。

sentences.en: And he comes into Washington, where the center of the cultural life in the Capitol is the Kennedy Center.
sentences.zh: 他来到华盛顿，而首都文化生活的中心就是肯尼迪中心。

sentences.en: And he's thinking, I'm the president now.
sentences.zh: 他在想，我现在是总统了。

sentences.en: So surely he'll be welcomed more broadly by the culture once he's in the White House.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦他入主白宫，肯定会受到文化界更广泛的欢迎。

sentences.en: But instead, that rejection really continued.
sentences.zh: 但相反，那种排斥真的持续下去了。

sentences.en: And there was probably no better example in that first year than the annual Kennedy Center Honors, which is the Kennedy Center's biggest night of the year.
sentences.zh: 在那第一年里，最好的例子莫过于一年一度的肯尼迪中心荣誉奖，这是肯尼迪中心一年中最盛大的夜晚。

sentences.en: And what form does that rejection take?
sentences.zh: 那种排斥是以什么形式表现出来的？

sentences.en: So three of the five honorees in 2017 said that they either would not come to the White House for the presentation of the actual medals before the ceremony at the Kennedy Center,
sentences.zh: 2017年五位获奖者中有三位表示，他们要么不会去白宫参加肯尼迪中心仪式前的奖章颁发仪式，

sentences.en: or they were considering not coming.
sentences.zh: 要么正在考虑不去。

sentences.en: Why did you decide not to do that?
sentences.zh: 你为什么决定不参加？

sentences.en: Because he's made me feel it's not my White House.
sentences.zh: 因为他让我觉得这不是我的白宫。

sentences.en: The first to say this was Norman Lear, who created All in the Family and many of our most beloved sitcoms and television shows.
sentences.zh: 第一个这么说的是诺曼·利尔，他创作了《全家福》以及我们许多最受欢迎的情景喜剧和电视节目。

sentences.en: But I've gotten over that.
sentences.zh: 但我已经克服了这一点。

sentences.en: It is my White House.
sentences.zh: 这是我的白宫。

sentences.en: It oughtn't to be his.
sentences.zh: 它不应该是他的。

sentences.en: And Carmen de Lavalade, a dancer and choreographer, said out now, no.
sentences.zh: 而舞蹈家兼编舞家卡门·德·拉瓦拉德说，不，不行。

sentences.en: I just can't.
sentences.zh: 我真的做不到。

sentences.en: I'm absolutely not going.
sentences.zh: 我绝对不会去。

sentences.en: I am 86 now.
sentences.zh: 我现在86岁了。

sentences.en: I have all these years I have done what anybody asked me to.
sentences.zh: 这么多年来，我一直按照别人的要求去做。

sentences.en: And this is the first time in my life I've ever said no.
sentences.zh: 这是我一生中第一次说不。

sentences.en: Lionel Richie, who was also an honoree that year, said, well...
sentences.zh: 那一年也是获奖者的莱昂内尔·里奇说，嗯……

sentences.en: You know, I'm going to just play it by ear.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我会见机行事。

sentences.en: I can't decide if I'll go.
sentences.zh: 我无法决定是否要去。

sentences.en: I must tell you, I'm not really happy as to what's going on right now with the controversies.
sentences.zh: 我必须告诉你，对于现在发生的争议，我真的不高兴。

sentences.en: And I think that that was quite a realization for him.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对他是相当大的打击。

sentences.en: He had gotten to the absolute top of our hierarchy and still that rejection continued.
sentences.zh: 他已经爬到了我们等级制度的最高层，但那种排斥依然存在。

sentences.en: So Trump's response to that was to say, okay, if you don't want me, I don't want you either.
sentences.zh: 所以特朗普对此的回应是，好吧，如果你不想要我，我也不想要你。

sentences.en: And he just was generally a no-show for the entirety of his four-year term.
sentences.zh: 在他四年的任期内，他基本上就是一个缺席者。

sentences.en: So for the next four years, Trump basically boycotts the Kennedy Center and thoroughly writes it off.
sentences.zh: 所以在接下来的四年里，特朗普基本上抵制了肯尼迪中心，并彻底否定了它。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so when he begins his second term in 2025, you know, this is now, he's newly energized.
sentences.zh: 所以当他在2025年开始第二个任期时，你知道，他现在焕然一新，充满活力。

sentences.en: He's got a different agenda when he comes in in his second term.
sentences.zh: 他在第二个任期开始时有不同的议程。

sentences.en: As we well know, he is vowing to be people's retribution.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所知，他誓言要成为人民的复仇者。

sentences.en: But he's also remaking aspects of society, including our cultural life.
sentences.zh: 但他也在重塑社会的各个方面，包括我们的文化生活。

sentences.en: He comes in as an anti-woke president.
sentences.zh: 他以一位反“觉醒”总统的身份上任。

sentences.en: He won on that.
sentences.zh: 他靠这个赢得了选举。

sentences.en: So barely in office for a month, 18 days to be exact, he starts to launch a plan to take over the Kennedy Center.
sentences.zh: 所以他上任才一个月，确切地说是18天，就开始启动接管肯尼迪中心的计划。

sentences.en: And take it over how?
sentences.zh: 怎么接管？

sentences.en: Just like logistically, what power does he have over it and how does he end up taking it over?
sentences.zh: 从后勤上讲，他对它有什么权力，他是如何最终接管它的？

sentences.en: So the president has the power to appoint board members to the Kennedy Center, and they basically oversee the running of the center itself.
sentences.zh: 总统有权任命肯尼迪中心的董事会成员，他们基本上负责监督中心的运营。

sentences.en: Typically, the board members serve six-year terms, so you had overlapping administration board members, appointees.
sentences.zh: 通常，董事会成员任期为六年，所以会有重叠的行政任命人员。

sentences.en: Democrats, Republicans, staggered.
sentences.zh: 民主党人、共和党人，交错任职。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they work together, and that was the way the Kennedy Center was designed.
sentences.zh: 他们一起工作，这就是肯尼迪中心的设计初衷。

sentences.en: But he came in and eliminated all of the Biden-era appointees wholesale and then stacked the board with people who were loyal to himself, his chief of staff, Susie Wiles,
sentences.zh: 但他上台后，全面清除了所有拜登时期的任命人员，然后用效忠于他的人填补了董事会，包括他的幕僚长苏西·怀尔斯，

sentences.en: the wife of the vice president, Usha Vance, Howard Lutnik's wife.
sentences.zh: 副总统的妻子乌莎·万斯，霍华德·卢特尼克的妻子。

sentences.en: And so they came in and took over the board.
sentences.zh: 于是他们进来接管了董事会。

sentences.en: And then their first move was to vote to replace the chairman with Mr. Trump.
sentences.zh: 他们的第一个举动就是投票罢免主席，由特朗普先生取而代之。

sentences.en: And the existing chairman, David Rubenstein, he had personally given $111 million to the Kennedy Center, its facilities, and its programming.
sentences.zh: 而现任主席大卫·鲁宾斯坦，他个人曾向肯尼迪中心捐赠了1.11亿美元，用于其设施和节目制作。

sentences.en: So immediately, the president replaces this mega philanthropist to the Kennedy Center with basically himself.
sentences.zh: 所以总统立即用他自己取代了这位肯尼迪中心的超级慈善家。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And what does chairman of the Kennedy Center, Trump, do with this newfound power?
sentences.zh: 那么作为肯尼迪中心主席的特朗普，用这新获得的权力做了什么？

sentences.en: It's a very exciting development.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常令人兴奋的发展。

sentences.en: So President Trump convenes a call with his new hand-picked board members.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统召集了他新挑选的董事会成员开会。

sentences.en: But he starts by bashing it as what he thinks it is.
sentences.zh: 但他首先抨击了它，表达了他对它的看法。

sentences.en: It got very wokey.
sentences.zh: 它变得太“觉醒”了。

sentences.en: A bastion of cultural elites.
sentences.zh: 是文化精英的堡垒。

sentences.en: And some people were not happy with it.
sentences.zh: 有些人对它不满意。

sentences.en: And some people refused to go.
sentences.zh: 有些人拒绝去那里。

sentences.en: And we're not going to have that.
sentences.zh: 我们不会允许这种情况发生。

sentences.en: Programming that everyday Americans aren't interested in and might even be offended by.
sentences.zh: 那些普通美国人不感兴趣，甚至可能感到被冒犯的节目。

sentences.en: And he's going to change all that.
sentences.zh: 他要改变这一切。

sentences.en: I think we're going to make it hot.
sentences.zh: 我想我们要让它变得火爆起来。

sentences.en: And we made the presidency hot.
sentences.zh: 我们让总统职位变得火爆了。

sentences.en: So this should be easy.
sentences.zh: 所以这应该很容易。

sentences.en: And make the Kennedy Center hot again.
sentences.zh: 让肯尼迪中心再次火爆起来。

sentences.en: So thank you all very much for your time.
sentences.zh: 所以非常感谢大家的时间。

sentences.en: I'm curious if there's any truth to what Trump is saying to this board.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇特朗普对董事会说的话是否有任何真实性。

sentences.en: Is it elitist?
sentences.zh: 它是精英主义的吗？

sentences.en: Does it have a left-wing tilt?
sentences.zh: 它有左倾倾向吗？

sentences.en: So I think here is where you realize what a radical misconception the president was laboring under.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在这里你会意识到总统陷入了多么激进的误解之中。

sentences.en: And partly due to the fact that for his entire first term, he didn't step foot in the Kennedy Center.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是他在整个第一个任期内，从未踏入过肯尼迪中心一步。

sentences.en: So it has a symphony.
sentences.zh: 它有交响乐团。

sentences.en: It has an opera.
sentences.zh: 它有歌剧院。

sentences.en: But the vast majority of its programming is meant to be entertainment, popular, works.
sentences.zh: 但其绝大多数节目都是为了娱乐，是大众化的作品。

sentences.en: I'll just, uh, I'll go backstage.
sentences.zh: 我只是，呃，我去后台看看。

sentences.en: Oh, that's okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，没关系。

sentences.en: That's okay.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: I know that song.
sentences.zh: 我知道那首歌。

sentences.en: That's about my favorite street.
sentences.zh: 那是关于我最喜欢的街道的。

sentences.en: So you're talking about performances like Big Bird and Sesame Street characters.
sentences.zh: 所以你指的是像《芝麻街》里的大鸟和角色那样的表演。

sentences.en: Aretha Franklin.
sentences.zh: 艾瑞莎·富兰克林。

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, Garth Brooks.
sentences.zh: 女士们，先生们，加斯·布鲁克斯。

sentences.en: Famous church chorale groups.
sentences.zh: 著名的教堂合唱团。

sentences.en: The Washington Ballet had its children's recital there.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿芭蕾舞团曾在那里举办过儿童汇演。

sentences.en: It was their chance to dance on the big stage.
sentences.zh: 那是他们在大舞台上表演的机会。

sentences.en: Local little kids doing ballet.
sentences.zh: 当地的小朋友们跳芭蕾。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Entire classes of school children came.
sentences.zh: 整个班级的学生都来了。

sentences.en: My own children's classes came.
sentences.zh: 我孩子所在的班级也来了。

sentences.en: Kids could run down the hall.
sentences.zh: 孩子们可以在大厅里奔跑。

sentences.en: The grand foyer, which is like two football fields long.
sentences.zh: 那个大门厅，足有两个足球场那么长。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: It was a wide open place.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常开阔的地方。

sentences.en: So, Elizabeth, how does Trump's decision to put his name on the Kennedy Center become, as you say, the beginning of the end for the center?
sentences.zh: 那么，伊丽莎白，特朗普决定把他的名字放在肯尼迪中心上，是如何成为你所说的中心终结的开始的呢？

sentences.en: Tell us about this legal battle.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲这场法律战。

sentences.en: So, on the Kennedy Center board, there are these so-called ex-officio members.
sentences.zh: 在肯尼迪中心董事会里，有所谓的当然成员。

sentences.en: They're members of Congress that could not be purged by the president when he remade the board.
sentences.zh: 他们是国会议员，在总统重组董事会时无法被清洗掉。

sentences.en: And one of them is Joyce Beatty, a congresswoman from Ohio.
sentences.zh: 其中一位是来自俄亥俄州的国会女议员乔伊斯·比蒂。

sentences.en: She filed suit after he renamed the center.
sentences.zh: 在他更名中心后，她提起了诉讼。

sentences.en: And her argument was that legally, this renaming could only be done by Congress.
sentences.zh: 她的论点是，在法律上，这种更名只能由国会来完成。

sentences.en: And what's her logic there?
sentences.zh: 那她的逻辑是什么？

sentences.en: Well, it's based in the center's origins.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是基于中心的起源。

sentences.en: So, back in the 1950s, when Dwight D.
sentences.zh: 回到20世纪50年代，当德怀特·D·

sentences.en: Eisenhower established what he wanted to be a globally recognized cultural center, it took an act of Congress to do that.
sentences.zh: 艾森豪威尔建立他想要的全球公认的文化中心时，这需要国会立法。

sentences.en: So, in 1958, Congress passed legislation establishing what was called the National Cultural Center.
sentences.zh: 所以，在1958年，国会通过了立法，建立了所谓的“国家文化中心”。

sentences.en: And that was its official name, the National Cultural Center.
sentences.zh: 那是它的官方名称，国家文化中心。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And when Kennedy was elected, he and First Lady, Jackie Kennedy, were big champions of the arts, and the performing arts in particular.
sentences.zh: 当肯尼迪当选时，他和第一夫人杰基·肯尼迪是艺术，特别是表演艺术的大力支持者。

sentences.en: So, they worked with Eisenhower and his wife, Mamie Eisenhower, to build support and funds for the new National Cultural Center.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们与艾森豪威尔及其夫人玛米·艾森豪威尔合作，为新的国家文化中心建立支持和筹集资金。

sentences.en: After Kennedy was assassinated, Congress stepped in again, and they renamed the National Cultural Center in Kennedy's honor as a living memorial to him.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪遇刺后，国会再次介入，他们以肯尼迪的名义将国家文化中心重新命名，作为对他活生生的纪念。

sentences.en: So, Congresswoman Beatty's argument is basically that because Congress turned this into a memorial to President Kennedy,
sentences.zh: 所以，比蒂议员的论点基本上是，因为国会将其变成了对肯尼迪总统的纪念，

sentences.en: only an act of Congress can change the name back or to something else.
sentences.zh: 只有国会法案才能将其改回原名或改为其他名称。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Not the president and not even the Kennedy Center's board, only Congress.
sentences.zh: 不是总统，甚至不是肯尼迪中心的董事会，只有国会。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, what happens with the lawsuit?
sentences.zh: 那么诉讼结果如何？

sentences.en: So, pretty swiftly, a court rules that Beatty is right, that it would take an act of Congress to rename the building.
sentences.zh: 很快，法院裁定比蒂是对的，重命名大楼需要国会法案。

sentences.en: And around the same time, the president, you know, hates this idea, of course.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，总统当然讨厌这个主意。

sentences.en: That his name would come off of it.
sentences.zh: 他的名字要被拿掉。

sentences.en: That his name would come off the building.
sentences.zh: 他的名字要从大楼上拿掉。

sentences.en: And so, when word spread of that, Washington had a whole day knowing that this was going to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以，当消息传开时，华盛顿整整一天都知道这件事要发生了。

sentences.en: And this festival-like crowd gathered to watch.
sentences.zh: 节日般的人群聚集在一起观看。

sentences.en: So, it was hundreds of people chanting, singing, you know, waiting for his name to come off.
sentences.zh: 有数百人高呼、唱歌，等待着他的名字被拿掉。

sentences.en: So, finally, they rolled scaffolding into place, and the crowd really went crazy, thinking, okay, this is finally going to happen.
sentences.zh: 最后，他们把脚手架推到位，人群真的疯狂了，心想，好吧，这终于要发生了。

sentences.en: And the director of the center could look out and see that this was something that the president wasn't really going to want to see on TV.
sentences.zh: 中心主任向外看去，意识到总统肯定不想在电视上看到这一幕。

sentences.en: So, then they started to unroll tarps that would obscure the entire operation of removing his name off the building.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始拉起防水布，遮挡拆除名字的整个过程。

sentences.en: Hide it, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是藏起来。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, behind the tarps, they started to take the letters off.
sentences.zh: 在防水布后面，他们开始拆除字母。

sentences.en: But they did this at 2.30, 3 o'clock in the morning.
sentences.zh: 但他们是在凌晨2点半、3点做的。

sentences.en: By that time, most of the crowd was gone.
sentences.zh: 到那时，大部分人群已经散去。

sentences.en: And so, there was a relative handful of us that could kind of sneak and peer around the edge of the tarps where they met the wall of the center.
sentences.zh: 所以，只有我们少数几个人能偷偷地从防水布与中心墙壁连接的边缘窥视。

sentences.en: That was really all you had a window into.
sentences.zh: 那真的是你唯一的观察窗口。

sentences.en: And then, beyond that, they left the tarps up, where they remain to this day.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，他们留下了防水布，直到今天还留在那里。

sentences.en: So, you could never see that his name had been removed.
sentences.zh: 所以你永远看不到他的名字已经被移除了。

sentences.en: But, of course, his name was removed, even if the removal remains hidden by a tarp.
sentences.zh: 但当然，他的名字确实被移除了，即使移除的过程被防水布遮盖着。

sentences.en: And given everything you've laid out in our conversation,
sentences.zh: 考虑到你在谈话中列出的所有事实，

sentences.en: I have to imagine that this was a really painful moment for Trump because his entire answer to this wounded relationship he had with the Kennedy Center was to take it over and to make it more and more his own.
sentences.zh: 我不得不认为这对特朗普来说是一个非常痛苦的时刻，因为他处理与肯尼迪中心这种受损关系的唯一方式，就是接管它，并让它越来越多地成为他自己的东西。

sentences.en: And for a brief shining moment, he literally has his name on the outside.
sentences.zh: 在短暂而辉煌的时刻，他的名字确实写在了外面。

sentences.en: The takeover is total and complete.
sentences.zh: 接管是彻底而完全的。

sentences.en: But now that is being taken from him.
sentences.zh: 但现在，这一切正在被从他手中夺走。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And you could see that by the emergence of a different argument vis-a-vis the Kennedy Center.
sentences.zh: 这一点从针对肯尼迪中心的不同论调的出现就能看出来。

sentences.en: And that was the president increasingly started to say that the center is in terrible disrepair.
sentences.zh: 总统开始越来越多地宣称该中心年久失修，状况堪忧。

sentences.en: And this was really ironic because a year prior, he had gotten $527 million from the big, beautiful bill to do renovations of the Kennedy Center.
sentences.zh: 这实在讽刺，因为就在一年前，他刚从那项宏大而美好的法案中获得了5.27亿美元，用于肯尼迪中心的翻新工程。

sentences.en: And Congress appropriates money every year for maintenance of the Kennedy Center.
sentences.zh: 而且国会每年都会为肯尼迪中心的维护拨款。

sentences.en: So, what was happening here?
sentences.zh: 那么，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: You know, in fact, the new director of the Kennedy Center, after Rick Grinnell departed, was a guy whose specialty, according to the president, he's a pro at construction.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在里克·格林内尔离职后，肯尼迪中心的新任主任是一位总统口中的“建筑专家”。

sentences.en: Why had this center suddenly become so dangerous as soon as this name came off the building that it would have to be closed?
sentences.zh: 为什么这个中心在名字从大楼上撤下后，突然就变得如此危险，以至于必须关闭？

sentences.en: So, if I'm reading between the lines of what you're saying here, it seems like once the president has lost the battle to have his name on the outside of the building,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我没理解错你的言外之意，似乎一旦总统在争取将自己的名字留在建筑外墙上的这场斗争中落败，

sentences.en: he begins to lose interest in the Kennedy Center functioning at all.
sentences.zh: 他就开始对肯尼迪中心的正常运作失去兴趣了。

sentences.en: Either it's mine or it's closed.
sentences.zh: 要么是我的，要么就关门。

sentences.en: And then he starts to go further and say, well, maybe it doesn't need just to be closed.
sentences.zh: 接着他变本加厉，说，嗯，也许不仅仅是关门那么简单。

sentences.en: Maybe the center will be demolished.
sentences.zh: 也许中心会被拆除。

sentences.en: It will be ripped down on social media, in comments to reporters.
sentences.zh: 他在社交媒体和对记者的评论中扬言要将其夷为平地。

sentences.en: He starts to raise the idea that it would be torn down completely.
sentences.zh: 他开始提出将其彻底拆除的想法。

sentences.en: All the presidents talk about the need for renovations and this rather drastic thought that perhaps the Kennedy Center should be demolished all seems to rest on the idea that the Kennedy Center is in really sad,
sentences.zh: 所有关于翻新必要性的讨论，以及这种认为肯尼迪中心应该被拆除的激进想法，似乎都建立在肯尼迪中心处于极其糟糕、

sentences.en: sorry, dangerous shape.
sentences.zh: 可悲且危险的状态这一前提之上。

sentences.en: Is that true?
sentences.zh: 这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Well, I'm not an engineer, but I can say that over the last few months, I've probably made 25 trips to the Kennedy Center.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不是工程师，但我可以说，在过去几个月里，我大概去了肯尼迪中心25次。

sentences.en: I never saw anything that suggested a serious danger to people's safety.
sentences.zh: 我从未发现任何迹象表明它对人们的安全构成了严重威胁。

sentences.en: But what happened earlier this month was that heavy storms in Washington brought down a five-foot chunk of plaster in the main foyer of the building.
sentences.zh: 但本月早些时候发生的事情是，华盛顿的一场大风暴导致大楼主门厅的一块五英尺长的石膏板掉落。

sentences.en: This is something that, you know, definitely needed to be repaired.
sentences.zh: 这确实是需要修复的地方。

sentences.en: But instead of just making that repair, they closed that enormous section of the building.
sentences.zh: 但他们没有仅仅进行修复，而是关闭了那一大片建筑区域。

sentences.en: They found security camera footage of the plaster actually falling, spread that around on social media.
sentences.zh: 他们找到了石膏掉落时的监控录像，并在社交媒体上大肆传播。

sentences.en: They measured the shards of plaster as they lay on the carpet.
sentences.zh: 他们测量了散落在地毯上的石膏碎片。

sentences.en: They measured the size of what they called a debris field, like this was a plane crash.
sentences.zh: 他们测量了所谓的“残骸区”的大小，搞得好像发生了空难一样。

sentences.en: Nobody cleaned up the mess left by the falling plaster for two weeks.
sentences.zh: 两周内，没人清理石膏掉落后留下的狼藉。

sentences.en: In the meantime, this chunk of plaster became a sort of politically tinged argument for giving the president what he wants, a closure of the place,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，这块石膏成了支持总统诉求——即关闭该场所——的一种带有政治色彩的论据，

sentences.en: which is exactly what happened on September 15th.
sentences.zh: 而这正是9月15日发生的事情。

sentences.en: The Kennedy Center board voted to close the building entirely.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪中心董事会投票决定彻底关闭该建筑。

sentences.en: Elizabeth, what's the impact of the Kennedy Center being totally closed now?
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白，肯尼迪中心现在完全关闭的影响是什么？

sentences.en: 2,500 people have lost their jobs.
sentences.zh: 2500人失业了。

sentences.en: There are no paid performances there any longer, where there used to be many in a day.
sentences.zh: 那里不再有付费演出，而过去每天都有很多场。

sentences.en: There are no tours.
sentences.zh: 没有了参观活动。

sentences.en: No one sees the exhibits, the art, anything.
sentences.zh: 没人能看到展览、艺术品或任何东西。

sentences.en: It's just the absolute antithesis of how Presidents Eisenhower and Kennedy and Congress conceived it.
sentences.zh: 这完全背离了艾森豪威尔总统、肯尼迪总统和国会当初的构想。

sentences.en: And that led to protests last week by thousands of people.
sentences.zh: 这导致上周成千上万的人进行了抗议。

sentences.en: This place has a lot of personal memories for me, times that I went on my first date here, came here with my family, came here with my husband.
sentences.zh: 这个地方承载了我许多个人回忆，我第一次约会是在这里，和家人来过这里，和丈夫也来过这里。

sentences.en: Who came just to say, sure, this needs to reopen, but also just to mourn all that had happened, that had gotten it to that point.
sentences.zh: 来的人不仅是为了说“当然，这里需要重新开放”，也是为了哀悼所有发生过的事情，以及导致它走到这一步的原因。

sentences.en: I played 18 hours Christmas music in the Grand Hall at Christmastime this last year.
sentences.zh: 去年圣诞节期间，我在大厅里演奏了18个小时的圣诞音乐。

sentences.en: People who had a lot of memories in the place.
sentences.zh: 这里承载了许多人的回忆。

sentences.en: Well, when my mom was alive, every Mother's Day we got her a ticket to the summer musical, and that was like an annual family tradition.
sentences.zh: 我母亲在世时，每个母亲节我们都会送她一张夏季音乐会的票，这就像是我们家的年度传统。

sentences.en: And they wanted to share what it meant to them.
sentences.zh: 他们想分享这个地方对他们的意义。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a beloved art space for all of us, an affordable option for many people if you couldn't afford to buy tickets.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这对我们所有人来说都是一个深受喜爱的艺术空间，对于那些买不起票的人来说，这是一个负担得起的选择。

sentences.en: It put the lie to the way the president had characterized the Kennedy Center, that it was a place that welcomed everybody, that really set out to bring people in,
sentences.zh: 这揭穿了总统对肯尼迪中心的描述，它本是一个欢迎所有人、真正致力于吸引人们参与的地方，

sentences.en: not to exclude them.
sentences.zh: 而不是排斥他们。

sentences.en: And at one point during the protest, people linked hands to form a human chain around the building.
sentences.zh: 抗议期间，人们手拉手在大楼周围形成了一道人链。

sentences.en: And it was like they were protecting something that was a living thing.
sentences.zh: 感觉他们是在保护一个有生命的东西。

sentences.en: And to them, it was a living thing.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，它确实是有生命的。

sentences.en: But now it was padlocked and closed and fenced off.
sentences.zh: 但现在它被锁住、关闭并围了起来。

sentences.en: The opera has moved elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 歌剧院已经搬到别处了。

sentences.en: They perform outside the Kennedy Center now.
sentences.zh: 他们现在在肯尼迪中心外面演出。

sentences.en: The symphony performs elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 交响乐团也在别处演出。

sentences.en: The performances that were there took years to book.
sentences.zh: 那里的演出都是提前几年预订的。

sentences.en: You're saying firing up this particular machine, if it were to happen even tomorrow, would take a very, very long time.
sentences.zh: 你是说，即使明天就能重新启动这台机器，也需要非常非常长的时间。

sentences.en: The arts just don't show up in a center like this on a dime.
sentences.zh: 艺术活动在这样的中心里不可能瞬间恢复。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And now that Trump has so thoroughly politicized it and personalized it, made the Kennedy Center entirely about himself, all that is gone.
sentences.zh: 现在特朗普已经将其彻底政治化和个人化，让肯尼迪中心完全变成了他自己的私产，这一切都消失了。

sentences.en: And there's no guarantee, even if it does return, that it could ever be the same as it was before.
sentences.zh: 而且即便它能回归，也无法保证能恢复到从前的样子。

sentences.en: Well, Elizabeth, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，伊丽莎白，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Lowe.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·洛。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的《Connections》谜题。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏吧。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.zh: 一些MSNOW的记者刚刚重新获得了进入白宫的权限，就在我们说话的时候。

sentences.en: On Thursday afternoon, reporters for CNN, Politico,
sentences.zh: 周四下午，CNN、Politico和MSNOW的记者在联邦法官几小时前裁定总统的禁令可能违宪后，获准重新进入白宫区域。

sentences.zh: 劳拉，如果你能听到我说话，我想立刻了解一下你的最新经历。

sentences.en: Laura, if you hear me, I want to get to you right away for the latest in what your experience has been.
sentences.zh: 是的，我听到了，彼得。

sentences.en: Yeah, I hear you, Peter.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚通过西北门获准回到白宫。

sentences.en: So I was just allowed back into the White House through the Northwest Gate.
sentences.zh: 特朗普对裁决的遵守，暂时结束了这场持续数日的新闻自由僵局。

sentences.en: Trump's compliance with the ruling brought to an end, for now, a days-long standoff over press freedom.
sentences.zh: 这场僵局引发了各大电视网罕见的协调抗议行动，他们拒绝像往常一样录制和发布总统的视频。

sentences.en: That standoff triggered a rare act of coordinated protest by major TV networks, which have refused to record and distribute video of the president as they usually do.

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
